title: Generation and use of functionalised hydrogels that can rapidly sample infected surfaces☆
author: Swift, Pinnock, et al.

steps.title: Prepare monomer solution and degas
steps.instruction: In a round‑bottom flask add glycerol monomethacrylate (GMMA, 5 g, 4.660 mL), glycidyl methacrylate (GME, 0.345 g, 0.321 mL) and ethylene glycol dimethacrylate (EGDMA, 0.206 g, 0.196 mL) together with isopropanol (2 mL); insert a magnetic stir bar and stir while bubbling dry nitrogen through the mixture for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Add photoinitiator and degas
steps.instruction: Add 2‑hydroxy‑2‑methylpropiphenone (HMPP, 55 mg) to the stirred solution and continue nitrogen bubbling for an additional 5 minutes.

steps.title: Inject mixture into quartz mold
steps.instruction: Using a glass syringe, inject the degassed monomer mixture into a mold formed by two 10 cm × 10 cm quartz plates separated by a 0.5 mm PTFE gasket and lined on the inner surfaces with a PET sheet (as shown in Diagram 1). Secure the plates with Bulldog clips.

steps.title: UV‑polymerize hydrogel sheet
steps.instruction: Place the assembled mold in a Dymax UV oven equipped with a 400 W metal‑halide UV‑A lamp and irradiate for 3 minutes; then turn the mold over and irradiate the opposite side for another 3 minutes.

steps.title: Wash cured hydrogel in IPA (5×1 h)
steps.instruction: Remove the cured hydrogel sheet from the mold, immerse it in fresh isopropanol and perform five consecutive washes, each lasting at least 1 hour, replacing the isopropanol each time.

steps.title: Aminate hydrogel with diamine
steps.instruction: Prepare a 20 % v/v solution of 1,3‑diaminopropane in isopropanol (total volume 250 mL). Submerge the hydrogel sheet in this solution for 48 hours, inverting the sheet after the first 24 hours.

steps.title: Post‑amine IPA washes (2×1 h)
steps.instruction: After the diamine treatment, wash the hydrogel twice in pure isopropanol, each wash lasting a minimum of 1 hour.

steps.title: Load functional polymers onto hydrogel
steps.instruction: In a sealable plastic container large enough to lay the hydrogel flat, dissolve 50 mg HB‑PNIPAM‑van, 100 mg HB‑PNIPAM‑pmx and 60 mg HB‑PNIPAM‑amp in 100 mL isopropanol. Add the hydrogel sheet, place the container on a low‑speed shaker and shake for 24 hours; flip the sheet, then shake for an additional 24 hours.

steps.title: Post‑loading IPA washes (2×1 h)
steps.instruction: Remove the hydrogel from the polymer solution and immerse it in pure isopropanol for 1 hour; replace the isopropanol with fresh solvent and repeat for a second 1‑hour wash.

steps.title: Deprotect polymyxin polymer
steps.instruction: Add 20 mL of a 20 % v/v piperidine‑in‑isopropanol solution to a sealable container, submerge the hydrogel sheet fully, and leave for 48 hours (overnight). Afterwards, wash the hydrogel in pure isopropanol for 1 hour, and repeat the pure‑IPA wash two more times (total three washes).

steps.title: Final PBS washes
steps.instruction: Wash the deprotected hydrogel three times with phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS), then incubate the hydrogel in the desired cell‑culture media before use.

steps.title: Characterize hydrogel properties
steps.instruction: Determine equilibrium water content (EWC) as described in the supporting information (expected ~61 % ± 4 %). Analyse residual monomer by soaking a hydrogel sample in methanol for 12 hours and performing GC on the supernatant. Record FTIR spectra and, if desired, image the material by scanning electron microscopy.
